name: Lunar South Pole — Shackleton Crater
source: NASA LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment (DLRE)

parameters.regolith_type: Basaltic anorthosite regolith, possible water-ice deposits (confirmed by LRO LAMP/LEND)
parameters.notes: Permanently shadowed region (PSR). Temperature extremes derived from LRO Diviner Channel 6/7 data. Ice confirmed by LCROSS impact. Zero atmosphere — vacuum environment. Solar irradiance near-zero in PSR.

Rover.notes: Extreme cold cycling degrades battery chemistry. Dust abrasion on wheel seals critical. Solar panels non-functional in PSR — requires RTG or beamed power.

EVA Suit.notes: Regolith electrostatic adhesion to visors. Suit joints risk cryogenic lock. CO2 scrubber thermal performance degraded. Radiation dose 1.84 mSv/day.

Habitat.notes: ISRU water-ice extraction viable. Regolith shielding mitigates radiation. Thermal management requires dedicated ATCS loops. Zero convective heat loss — only radiative.

name: Jezero Crater — Mars
source: NASA MRO CRISM / Perseverance Rover MEDA Instrument / NASA PDS

parameters.regolith_type: Iron-oxide basalt, olivine-carbonate minerals, ancient deltaic sediment (confirmed CRISM/SHERLOC)
parameters.notes: Ancient crater lake delta. Temperature from Perseverance MEDA diurnal records. Thin CO2 atmosphere (95.3% CO2). Dust storms can drop irradiance by 50%. ISRU potential: MOXIE-heritage O2 extraction.

Rover.notes: Dust accumulation on solar panels reduces power 10-40%. CO2 atmosphere allows minor convective cooling. Rocky deltaic terrain — wheel stress. Dust storm season operational protocols required.

EVA Suit.notes: Atmospheric pressure ~600 Pa — same suit design as lunar with CO2 scrubber priority. Fine dust (<3 µm) penetrates seals. UV + GCR + SEP radiation hazard.

Habitat.notes: ISRU: MOXIE-heritage O2 from CO2 atmosphere. Regolith sintering/concrete construction viable. Perchlorate soil contamination hazard for life support systems.
